title: Lemon Drizzle Cake
subtitle: Moist lemon sponge with a crunchy sugar crust
excerpt: A light, moist lemon sponge baked in a loaf tin, then pierced all over and drenched with a sharp lemon and sugar drizzle while still warm. The drizzle soaks in and sets into a crunchy, crystalline crust.

recipe.sourceNotes: Lemon drizzle cake is one of the most popular British bakes, a feature of every school fete, church sale, and tearoom in the country. The recipe is essentially a simple all-in-one sponge cake, distinguished by the drizzle applied immediately after baking: a mixture of lemon juice and caster sugar poured over the hot cake while it is still in the tin. The lemon juice keeps the cake moist and the sugar crystallises on the surface as it dries, creating the characteristic crunchy, sweet-sharp crust. The cake is at its best the day after baking, once the drizzle has been absorbed and the flavours have settled. Unwaxed lemons give more juice and the zest is usable without chemical treatment.

recipeTools.notes: A 900 g (2 lb) loaf tin, lined.

content.text: The drizzle must go on while the cake is still hot from the oven: if the cake cools first, the drizzle will not soak in properly and will pool on the surface. Pierce the cake all over with a skewer before pouring the drizzle. Use the full amount of lemon juice: it should seem like a lot, but the cake needs it to stay moist.

items.preparation: unwaxed, finely grated zest and juice

content.text: Heat the oven to 180 C / fan 160 C / gas 4. Grease and line a 900 g loaf tin. Beat the butter and 225 g caster sugar together until pale and fluffy. Add the eggs one at a time, beating well after each. Fold in the flour, lemon zest, and milk.
Spoon into the prepared tin and level the surface. Bake for 45 to 50 minutes until a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean.

While the cake bakes, mix the lemon juice with the 75 g caster sugar. As soon as the cake comes out of the oven, pierce it all over with a skewer down to the base. Spoon the drizzle slowly over the hot cake so it soaks in. Leave to cool completely in the tin. Turn out and slice.
